Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.

Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.

With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.

Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.

About the Role

As a software engineering intern, you will work closely with leading experts in the field of machine learning, robotics, and software. Depending on your skill sets and areas of interest, you will work on some or all of the following: Data Platform, Onboard Systems, ML Infrastructure, Simulation, or Technical Infrastructure teams.

About the Work

Depending on your skill set and areas of interest you will work on some or all of the following:

- Data Platform: The Data Platform serves as a comprehensive management system for Nuro AI Driver's data, labels, and metrics, facilitating seamless access functionality. The team focuses on data annotation across various domains, including 2D/3D perception, mapping, behavior trajectory, and language/text. It also handles data ingestion and mining, employing methods such as heuristics and embedding search. Additionally, the platform supports the autonomy evaluation infrastructure by providing detailed introspection.

- Onboard Systems: Our onboard system team’s software engineers provide a reliable and high-performance platform that allows our autonomy teams to integrate their autonomy software and algorithms that work across various self-driving platforms. This work requires close collaboration with our software teams, hardware teams, and systems/safety team to make sure new software and hardware work together safely and reliably and resolve onboard error and performance problems.

- ML Infrastructure: The ML Infra team is the accelerator to our ML-first autonomy strategy. This team provides solutions to empower machine learning development in Nuro and optimize on-cloud training and onboard inference. Our solutions include a distributed training platform, ML compiler, model components libraries, e.t.c. The team provides opportunities for infra engineers to work fully embedded in ML teams to build cutting edge deep learning technologies.

- Simulation: The Simulation team builds the simulator that allows us to develop and test our autonomous driving technology in a virtual setting. We work on the core simulator and simulation frameworks, sensor simulation, scenario generation, and solutions that combine real-world data with synthetic techniques to push the boundaries of what can be simulated, collaborating closely with teams across Autonomy and AI Platform to allow us to simulate realistically and reliably at scale.

- Technical Infrastructure: this group owns few fundamental services for entire engineering organizations: generic compute platform to host mission-critical workflows such as data processing and simulation, storage management service which manages hundreds of PB of data, cloud infrastructure serves as IaaC which provisions and maintains all cloud resources, engineering productivity provides tools such as build and CI/CD to make engineering work more efficient.

About You

You have deep expertise and prior experience in some or many of the following areas:

- You are a current BS or MS candidate in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field graduating in June 2027 or later

- You have experience in one or more of the following areas: backend API design, applications development, large-scale distributed systems; data storage and processing systems; advanced algorithms using C++ and Python; machine learning, multithreading; x86 architecture; and software performance tuning and optimization, robotics software frameworks, different compute modalities (CPU, GPU, FPGA) etc.

- You have strong problem solving and programming skills.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

The Palantir Design Team is responsible for the human experience of using our software. Our team is growing rapidly, but we're committed to creating a tight-knit team environment that fosters trust, integrity, empathy, and growth. We work together in realizing a shared product vision, and regularly give feedback and critique to each other.

Designing at Palantir is a varied experience. On a given day, you might be: leading a design sprint for your product team; designing a micro-interaction to make a complex analytical task feel simple; and/or advocating for UX consistency by creating flexible, reusable UI components.

Designers at Palantir develop a deep understanding of the problems our customers face while solving some of the world’s most unique challenges. Our mission is to build generalizable and scalable solutions that elegantly handle the complexity of these problem spaces.

Core Responsibilities

- Interaction and visual design. As a product designer, you'll be involved at every stage of design work. You'll help define early product concepts, flesh out the high-level workflow and micro-interactions of a feature, and execute on a crisp and effective visual design. You should have experience designing and prototyping using tools such as Figma.

- User research. We frequently do informal user research, and value people who can be flexible with research processes and methodologies to achieve the right outcome. You'll often visit customer offices to interview and learn from the users we serve. You'll pair qualitative methods (e.g. scripted usability tests and contextual inquiry) with quantitative information, like product and usage metrics.

- Deliver and communicate designs in close collaboration. We work closely with product and forward deployed engineers to realize our design ideas. You'll treat engineers and product managers as partners and collaborate with them to prototype and build out products.

- Awareness of how software interfaces are built. Familiarity with HTML, CSS, Javascript, and Typescript is appreciated. You don't need to be an expert—just fluent enough to collaborate with engineers, and know what's possible with frontend technologies.

- Designers at Palantir have great autonomy over their work, so a wide skill set is necessary. However, many designers on the team are also passionate experts in one area. You might be the kind of designer who ships code every week, or the kind of designer who shares detailed user research findings with your team.

What We Value

- Excellent collaboration and communication skills with the ability to build great relationships with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders, and convey and debate design rationale.

- High empathy and dedication to the user, striving to understand and empower them.

- An iterative design process. You validate your ideas early (with stakeholders and users) and are thoughtful and intentional in seeking and responding to feedback. You move fast, listen, and adapt. You rapidly incorporate feedback, and prioritize collaboration. You are adept at giving and receiving critiques.

- Excitement for solving hard, complex problems. You are excited to design for technically complex and data dense interfaces. You thrive in an environment where you can jump into deep subject matter expertise to define simple, approachable, yet still powerful product experiences.

- Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions when needed.

What We Require

- Train and evaluate models in PyTorch using both simulated data and data captured over the air.

- Detail your results and contribute to publications, patents, and internal technical reports.

- Strong background in AI/ML for wireless communications.
- Solid understanding of ISAC concepts and waveforms, such as OFDM-based sensing.

Company Description

The Robot Learning Lab at the Bosch Center for Artificial Intelligence (BCAI) in Pittsburgh invites research interns to help build robots that acquire transferable skills, adapt to unfamiliar situations, and improve through real-world experience. Working at the intersection of robot learning, multimodal machine learning, embodied AI, and generative AI, we turn challenging robotics and automation problems into fundamental scientific investigations with industrial impact. Our goal is to develop reliable robotic systems that augment human capabilities and collaborate with people and other agents.

Research opportunities span:

- Robot foundation models: vision–language–action models, test-time adaptation and steering, and learning from deployment experience and failures.

- Agentic robot systems: coding agents and multi-agent frameworks for skill discovery, composition, long-horizon planning, and robot control.

- Dexterous and contact-rich manipulation: integrating vision, touch, and proprioception for precise interaction with rigid and deformable objects.

- Transferable robot skills: cross-embodiment representation learning, learning from human and robot demonstrations, and retrieval-based policy generalization.

- Simulation and world modeling: generative digital twins and Real2Sim2Real pipelines for policy learning, evaluation, and transfer to physical robots.

We combine Bosch’s industrial research environment with close collaborations across the Robotics Institute at Carnegie Mellon University, including dual affiliations among lab members. Interns help shape research questions, develop new methods, and evaluate systems in simulation and on physical robots, with the aim of publishing at leading robotics and machine learning venues. Across projects, we emphasize rigorous experimentation, effective use of open-source models and tools, and a clear path from scientific insight to practical robotic capability.

Job Description

We seek research interns who combine strong scientific judgment with the initiative to take ownership of an ambitious research project. Working closely with their mentors and collaborators, interns will formulate compelling research questions, critically assess prior work, develop and implement new methods, and design experiments that produce clear, defensible scientific insights.

Successful candidates will bring strong foundations in machine learning and robotics, with depth in one or more of the following areas:

- Generalization and transfer: learning multimodal representations and robot policies that transfer across tasks, objects, environments, and embodiments, including settings with limited demonstrations or deployment data.

- Policy learning and robot foundation models: imitation learning, reinforcement learning, generative policies, and the training, fine-tuning, or post-training of vision–language–action and other embodied foundation models.

- Learning at deployment: test-time adaptation, policy steering, failure detection and recovery, and agentic frameworks for reasoning, skill composition, and continued improvement.

- Data and simulation: combining human demonstrations, robot trajectories, and synthetic data; developing simulation or world-model-based pipelines for training, evaluation, and transfer to physical robots.

- Effective implementation: translating research ideas into reliable software, implementing and debugging neural policies, and using efficient training, inference, and distributed GPU workflows where appropriate.

- Rigorous evaluation: selecting informative baselines and ablations, diagnosing failures and distribution shifts, examining dataset biases, and characterizing robustness, data efficiency, and generalization.

Interns will collaborate with teammates to develop research contributions for publication at leading venues and contribute to invention disclosures and patent applications arising from their work.

Tasks

- Define a focused research problem with mentors and collaborators, connecting an important scientific question to a meaningful robotics or automation challenge.

- Critically review relevant literature, identify limitations in existing approaches, and articulate a testable research hypothesis.

- Develop an R&D plan specifying the proposed methods, data sources, experimental settings, evaluation metrics, milestones, and target publication venues.

- Design and implement the proposed approach, maintaining reproducible code, documented experimental configurations, and clear records of results.

- Evaluate methods in simulation and on physical robots through quantitative comparisons, targeted ablations, qualitative analysis, and theoretical analysis where appropriate.

- Share progress, relevant literature, experimental findings, and open challenges in weekly discussions; refine the research plan as evidence emerges.

- Prepare a research manuscript with collaborators for submission to venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICRA, IROS, Science Robotics, IJRR, T-RO, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, etc., and contribute to associated technical reports and patent materials.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Ph.D., or a recent postdoctoral researcher, in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field.

- Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or equivalent.

- Strong foundations in machine learning and robot learning, including representation learning, policy learning, optimization, and experimental design.

- Hands-on experience training or adapting modern robot policies and foundation models, such as vision-language-action (VLA) transformers with autoregressive action-token prediction or diffusion/flow-matching action heads for continuous action-chunk generation, or world action models (WAMs) that jointly predict future observations and robot actions. Relevant training experience includes multi-task pretraining or behavior cloning/supervised fine-tuning with action-token cross-entropy, diffusion denoising, conditional flow-matching, or joint video-action prediction objectives; or offline or online reinforcement learning post-training using actor-critic or policy-gradient methods.

- Strong Python programming skills; experience implementing, debugging, and evaluating neural models using PyTorch or a comparable framework; and hands-on experience using coding agents to develop, test, and maintain robotics and machine learning software, including reviewing and validating agent-generated code.

- Practical experience with physical robot platforms, including robot data collection, policy deployment, and closed-loop experimentation.

- Ability to design rigorous evaluations using appropriate baselines, ablations, and diagnostic analyses to characterize generalization, robustness, and failure modes.

- Demonstrated research ownership, supported by publications, preprints, or substantial research projects, together with clear technical communication and effective collaboration.

Desired Qualifications

- Experience training or adapting robot foundation models using heterogeneous human demonstrations, robot trajectories, and synthetic data, including data curation, quality assessment, and cross-embodiment transfer.

- Experience integrating large language models, vision–language models, or other multimodal foundation models into robot perception, planning, control, or evaluation workflows.

- Experience with test-time adaptation, policy steering, embodied memory, failure detection and recovery, or agentic systems that generate, execute, and refine robot skills.

- Experience in dexterous or contact-rich manipulation, including learning from visual, tactile, force, proprioceptive, or acoustic feedback.

- Experience with simulation, generative world models, digital twins, or Real2Sim2Real pipelines for policy training, evaluation, and transfer.

- Experience with multi-GPU or multi-node training, efficient fine-tuning and inference, and reproducible workflows encompassing versioned datasets, experiment tracking, and checkpoint management.

- Proficiency developing robotics and machine learning software on Linux, using version control and maintainable software practices.

- Theoretical depth in areas such as transfer learning, reinforcement learning, optimization, uncertainty estimation, or safe learning and control.

- A strong publication record at leading robotics, machine learning, or computer vision venues, particularly contributions demonstrating methodological depth and careful empirical validation.

Additional Information

We Are Bosch.

- Use scripting and validation tools to improve test repeatability, collect results, and analyze failures.
